requestedActions.title: List active task titles from the connected person's Todoist account, including all pages of results

guide.summary: Todoist documents OAuth authorization with a scope parameter. For a read-only task listing, the documented read scope data:read covers tasks, and GET /api/v1/tasks lists active tasks with cursor pagination. Obtain a client ID, authorize with data:read only, and test the first page and one continuation page with a representative test account. Registration location, token exchange details and the stop condition for task pagination are not in the supplied sources. Customer distribution to other workspaces has no supplied review or approval evidence, so that path stays unknown.

findings.title: OAuth authorization is documented for this integration
findings.detail: Todoist documents OAuth setup and an authorization URL that takes client_id, scope, state and response_type=code. Users are redirected to that URL to authorize the app.

evidence.quote: Easy setup: OAuth in a minute.
https://app.todoist.com/oauth/authorize?client_id = 0123456789abcdef & scope = data:read,data:delete & state = secretstring & response_type = code
Redirect users to the authorization URL at the endpoint

findings.title: Request data:read for reading active tasks
findings.detail: data:read grants read-only access to application data, including tasks. It is the documented scope for the listing action.
findings.appliesWhen: Customer connects an individual Todoist account for task listing

evidence.quote: data:read Grants read-only access to application data, including tasks, projects, labels, and filters.
Get Tasks Get all active tasks for the user.
get /api/v1/tasks https://api.todoist.com /api/v1/tasks

findings.title: Avoid data:read_write and write scopes
findings.detail: data:read_write includes write access and is not needed for a read-only listing. Write-capable scopes such as task:add and data:delete must not be requested.

evidence.quote: data:read_write Grants read and write access to application data, including tasks, projects, labels, and filters. This scope includes task:add and data:read scopes.
data:delete Grants permission to delete application data, including tasks, labels, and filters.

findings.title: Pagination uses a cursor from the previous response
findings.detail: Fetch the first page without a cursor, then pass next_cursor as the cursor parameter. Keep the same parameters on every page.

evidence.quote: To fetch the first page of results, make a request without a cursor parameter:
Subsequent Requests To fetch the next page, include the cursor parameter with the value from next_cursor :
Important : Always use the same parameters (filters, sorting, etc.) when using a cursor. Changing parameters between paginated requests may result in unexpected behavior or errors.

evidence.quote: https://app.todoist.com/oauth/authorize?client_id = 0123456789abcdef & scope = data:read,data:delete & state = secretstring & response_type = code

steps.title: Implement the authorization redirect and callback
steps.detail: Build the authorize redirect with scope=data:read, a random state value and response_type=code. Build the callback that checks state. Do not implement any write scope.
steps.doneWhen: The redirect URL contains only the data:read scope and the callback rejects a mismatched state.

evidence.quote: https://app.todoist.com/oauth/authorize?client_id = 0123456789abcdef & scope = data:read,data:delete & state = secretstring & response_type = code
Redirect users to the authorization URL at the endpoint
data:read Grants read-only access to application data, including tasks, projects, labels, and filters.

steps.title: Authorize the representative test account
steps.detail: Sign in with the representative Todoist test account and approve data:read. Exchange the returned code for an access token using the documented token step. Confirm the consent screen lists only the read scope.
steps.doneWhen: An OAuth access token is obtained for the test account and the consent screen shows only the read scope.

evidence.quote: https://app.todoist.com/oauth/authorize?client_id = 0123456789abcdef & scope = data:read,data:delete & state = secretstring & response_type = code
data:read Grants read-only access to application data, including tasks, projects, labels, and filters.

steps.title: Test the first page of active tasks
steps.detail: Call GET /api/v1/tasks with the OAuth token. Expect HTTP 200 with a results array and next_cursor. Boundary check: confirm the request is a GET only, that the token shows data:read, and that the request log contains no POST, PUT or DELETE.
steps.doneWhen: First page returns results with task content and next_cursor, and the request log shows only GET.

evidence.quote: Get Tasks Get all active tasks for the user.
curl "https://api.todoist.com/api/v1/tasks?limit=50" \ -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_TOKEN"

steps.title: Test the continuation page with the next cursor
steps.detail: Repeat the same request with the same parameters and cursor set to next_cursor from the prior page. Continue while next_cursor is present. Expect results with no duplicate task IDs. Boundary check: verify the same read-only GET pattern and that only listing requests were sent.
steps.doneWhen: At least one continuation page is retrieved with the same parameters, and the stop condition for tasks is confirmed.

evidence.quote: Subsequent Requests To fetch the next page, include the cursor parameter with the value from next_cursor :
curl "https://api.todoist.com/api/v1/tasks?cursor=eyJwYWdlIjoyLCJsaW1pdCI6NTB9.aGFzaA&limit=50" \ -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_TOKEN"
Important : Always use the same parameters (filters, sorting, etc.) when using a cursor. Changing parameters between paginated requests may result in unexpected behavior or errors.
